title: Project: Student Grade Manager
learningObjectives: Model student identity and assessment data with suitable types
Validate scores against the documented allowed numeric range
Calculate averages without dividing by an empty collection
Assign grades using explicit and non-overlapping score boundaries
Produce readable student summaries and test boundary scores

understand.concept: Keep score validation separate from grade calculation, and define whether grade boundaries are inclusive. A collection can hold records, while methods make each operation testable.
understand.whyItMatters: Project: Student Grade Manager helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain. It connects core language knowledge with realistic programming tasks.
understand.analogy: Treat this concept as a clearly labeled tool: select it for a specific responsibility and check the result.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a learning aid; actual behavior is defined by Java language rules and API contracts.

explain.narrative:
## Model students and assessment data

Represent each student with a stable identifier, a name and one or more assessment scores. A Java record is suitable for a simple immutable data carrier; a class is appropriate when the object must enforce rules while its state changes. Decide whether the project stores individual scores or only a final score, and keep that decision consistent.

## Validate before calculating

If scores use a 0–100 scale, reject values below 0 or above 100 before storing them. Define grade boundaries explicitly and avoid overlapping conditions. If grade A begins at 90, a score of exactly 90 belongs to A; document the other inclusive ranges too. Do not calculate an average for an empty score list: report that no scores are available or return a clearly defined optional result.

## Calculate and present a useful summary

Use a numeric type and an intentional rounding policy for averages. Keep validation, average calculation, grade assignment and display in separate methods. Store students in a List when their order matters; sort a copy or use a comparator for a ranked display so entry order is not unexpectedly changed. Decide how duplicate student IDs are handled before adding a student.

## Test boundary conditions

Test no students, one student, multiple scores, a score exactly at every grade boundary, invalid scores, duplicate IDs and a student with no assessments. Check both the calculated value and displayed grade. The project is complete when its rules are explicit and tests demonstrate them, not merely when a sample list prints successfully.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] scores = {80, 90, 100}; int total = 0; for (int score : scores) total += score; System.out.println(total / scores.length); } }

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int score = 85; String grade = score >= 90 ? "A" : score >= 80 ? "B" : score >= 70 ? "C" : "D"; System.out.println(grade); } }
examples.explanation: Maps a validated score to a grade band.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int score = 105; System.out.println(score >= 0 && score <= 100 ? "valid" : "invalid"); } }
examples.explanation: Rejects a score outside the permitted range.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { record Student(String name, int score) {} Student s = new Student("Mira", 92); System.out.println(s.name() + ": " + s.score()); } }
examples.explanation: Uses a record to represent a student result.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] scores = {65, 72, 88}; int passed = 0; for (int s : scores) if (s >= 70) passed++; System.out.println("passed=" + passed); } }
examples.explanation: Produces a summary count using a clear passing threshold.

practise.guidedTask: Create a Student record with an ID, name and score. Validate score range, calculate the average and assign grades using documented inclusive boundaries.
practise.independentTask: Build a grade manager that accepts multiple students, stores them in a List, and prints a sorted summary with each student's average and grade.
hints: Define inclusive grade boundaries and the policy for students with no scores before coding.
Validate every score and student ID before adding or updating the stored record.
Test exact grade boundaries, empty collections, duplicate IDs and invalid scores.
practise.challenge: Test no students, one student, a score exactly on every grade boundary, invalid scores and duplicate student IDs.

questions.prompt: Why should student scores be validated before calculating grades?
options: To reject values outside the allowed score range
To make every student receive the same grade
questions.answer: To reject values outside the allowed score range
questions.explanation: Range validation prevents impossible scores from entering the data set and distorting averages or grade assignments.

questions.prompt: How is an average commonly calculated?
options: Sum the scores and divide by the number of scores
Multiply the scores by the count
Divide the count by the sum
questions.answer: Sum the scores and divide by the number of scores
questions.explanation: An average is the sum of the included scores divided by the number of scores; the empty case must be handled separately.

options: To avoid gaps or overlaps at cutoff values
questions.answer: To avoid gaps or overlaps at cutoff values
questions.explanation: Explicit inclusive grade boundaries ensure every allowed score maps to exactly one grade without gaps or overlaps.

questions.prompt: What should happen when there are no scores?
options: Handle the empty case instead of dividing by zero
questions.answer: Handle the empty case instead of dividing by zero
questions.explanation: With no scores, the program must avoid dividing by zero and report or represent the absence of assessment data deliberately.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility should be separated from grade calculation?
questions.explanation: Console input and presentation should be separated from grade calculation so the calculation can be tested independently.
